items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: So we became fast friends, Sidney and I

ctx.x: Well, back to Sidney Catlett. I first met him when he was with Louis Armstrong's big band, had our association during his days with Louie's small band. And he was playing on 52nd Street also during the heydays when I was with Don Bias of the Three Deuces, he would be with Don at other times when I was possibly with Ben Webster, and later when I was with Ben Webster at the Famous Door, Sidney Catlett was with Don Bias. And when I was at the Famous Door with Ben Webster -- I must remember later on to tell you this,…

So we became fast friends, Sidney and I, and I mentioned with whom and where he played so you can understand I had a long time and many chances to observe this man. A large man, well over six feet -- long arms, and extraordinary large hands. When he sat down at the drums, the drumsticks looked like toothpicks in his hand. You expected to hear a thunderous eruption from the drums. Instead, well, a soft, fluid flow of assorted sounds emanated.
Whatever the music called for -- let's put it that
